record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes a static weight-edit version of direction removal and explicitly claims refusals were removed, but it does not report results for the original all-layer, all-position activation ablation or direction addition.
record.gate_note: The README explicitly claims the edit removed refusals and gives coding benchmark scores. The suggested held-out refusal-rate check and its expected result (~0%) are run instructions, not reported measurements. Candidate-layer selection details and tuning suggestions are not results.
record.test_reason: The repo applies the original weight-orthogonalization edit to a new model, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, and asserts the edit removed refusals. That assertion is the only evidence on V2: it gives no refusal rate, prompt set or counts. T3 (new model setting) fits better than T2, because the method is the original paper's own weight-edit form, not a different method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim abliteration removed refusals without breaking coding ability, with an average delta of about −0.6 points. The paraphrase should add that the base scores are cited from the Qwen tech report rather than measured in the same run, and that the abliterated scores also include Q4_K_M quantization.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repository; describes estimating a harmful-minus-harmless direction at the last prompt token, selecting a layer, and permanently orthogonalizing residual-writing weights. It does not report the original activation intervention's results.
record.method_sensitivity: The README suggests varying candidate layers, sample count, and harmful prompt set if refusals survive, but reports no outcomes for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The abliterated Q4_K_M model scores 89.6/84.8/91.3/77.0 on HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+. The comparison base scores are 92.7/87.2/90.2/75.1, cited from the tech report.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Abliteration plus 4-bit quantization of Qwen2.5-Coder-32B leaves coding pass@1 within about 3 points of the reported base scores.

record.problems: The README gives no refusal-rate numbers or evaluation-set details. It does not establish that the described pipeline was run; the suggested refusal-rate check is an instruction, and benchmark uncertainty is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The README's expected ~0% refusal-rate line is a run instruction, not a reported result.

untested.parts: Any quantified refusal rate before and after the edit, the evaluation prompt set, and confirmation that the released model was actually evaluated.
Activation ablation at every layer and position, and direction addition; per-layer hook ablation is only used to select a layer, with no results reported.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool repository with 1 star; the code was not run. The V2 support depends entirely on one unquantified sentence. The capability comparison is against a cited baseline, despite the 'apples-to-apples' wording.

versions.untested_parts: No reported result for causal activation ablation at every layer and position, direction addition, or the original intervention's effects.
No numerical refusal rate, prompt-set details, or confirmation that the model was actually released are reported.
No jailbreak suppression or robustness-training result.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer result.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
